obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: The credit union reasonably believes it has experienced a reportable cyber incident: a substantial cyber incident causing a substantial loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of a network or member information system from unauthorized access to or exposure of sensitive data; a disruption of operations or vital member services from a cyberattack; or a disruption or unauthorized access through a compromise of a CUSO, cloud service provider, other third-party data host, or the supply chain
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the credit union reasonably believes a reportable cyber incident occurred; for a third-party compromise under (c)(1)(i)(C), within 72 hours of the third party's notice if sooner
notify: NCUA-designated point of contact (email, telephone, or other method NCUA prescribes)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federally insured credit union; in force since 2023-09-01 (88 FR 12811). In the BEC scenario, attacker access to the Member Services mailbox holding members' Social Security numbers is likely reportable; the ISO and the President and CEO record the decision and time either way (POL-03 4.4)

obligation: Notice to the NCUA Regional Director of unauthorized access to sensitive member information
trigger: Credit union becomes aware of an incident involving unauthorized access to or use of sensitive member information (name, address, or phone with SSN, driver's license, account or card number, or a password or PIN permitting account access; or log-in credentials)
deadline: As soon as possible
notify: NCUA Regional Director (a state supervisory authority only for state-chartered credit unions)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - make this notice together with the 748.1(c) report when both apply. Federal charter, so no state supervisor notice

obligation: Member notice under the response program
citation: 12 CFR 748, Appendix B III.A to III.C (guidance)
trigger: Reasonable investigation shows misuse of a member's sensitive information has occurred or is reasonably possible
deadline: As soon as possible; delay only if law enforcement determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
notify: Affected members (clear and conspicuous notice with the III.B content, by phone, mail, or email for members who agreed to electronic notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - in the BEC scenario misuse occurred for the member whose wire was diverted and is reasonably possible for members whose documents were in the mailbox. NCUA encourages notifying the nationwide consumer reporting agencies before a large mailing (III.B.2)

obligation: Suspicious activity report
trigger: Known or suspected federal crime against or through the credit union: any amount for insider abuse; $5,000 or more with an identifiable suspect; $25,000 or more regardless of suspect
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection; if no suspect is identified on that date, up to 30 more days to identify one, never more than 60 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA Officer. A fraudulent wire of $25,000 or more always requires a SAR (748.1(d)(1)(iii)). SARs are confidential (748.1(d)(5)); keep the copy and supporting documents 5 years (748.1(d)(3))

obligation: Immediate notice of a violation needing immediate attention
trigger: A reportable violation that needs immediate attention, such as an ongoing scheme
deadline: Immediately, by telephone, in addition to the SAR
notify: An appropriate law enforcement authority and NCUA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker is still active (for example more fraudulent requests or continued mailbox access)

obligation: Board notice of SAR filing
trigger: A SAR is filed
deadline: Promptly after filing
notify: Board of Directors or the committee it designates
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA Officer reports at the next board meeting or sooner

obligation: Catastrophic act report
trigger: Disaster causing physical damage or an interruption of vital member services projected to last more than two consecutive business days
deadline: Within 5 business days; keep a record at the main office
applies_at_this_tier: Not in a BEC incident; kept for ransomware or hurricane scenarios. NCUA has proposed changes (90 FR 60591), not final

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; fast reporting improves the chance of freezing funds
notify: FBI through ic3.gov; local FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but part of the runbook; supports the SAR and any law enforcement delay request

obligation: Wire recall request to the beneficiary bank
citation: Payment system practice; wire service agreement with the corporate credit union (contract)
trigger: A wire the credit union sent is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery; before the beneficiary bank releases funds
notify: Corporate credit union wire desk (recall message), then the beneficiary bank's fraud department
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Operations Manager. Not a legal notice, but the most time-critical step

obligation: Refund of an unauthorized payment order
trigger: A payment order accepted in the member's name was not authorized and is not effective as the member's order, for example because no agreed security procedure (callback) was followed
deadline: Refund with interest from the date the credit union received payment; counsel determines effectiveness under 670.202
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consumer wires through Fedwire or a similar system are excluded from Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.3(c)(3)), so Article 4A governs. Counsel decides; the missing written security procedure is central

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of a Florida individual (name with SSN, driver license or ID number, financial account number with a required access code or password; or a user name or email with a password)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Notice under the guidelines of the primary federal regulator (NCUA Appendix B) is deemed compliant if members are notified in accordance with those guidelines
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day date; counsel confirms the Appendix B notice meets the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals). A credit union that timely sends the Department a copy of its Appendix B notice is deemed compliant with subsection (3)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida individuals; not in the worked example (398)

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: Credit union decides notice is not required because, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; sent to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if relied on; not expected when Social Security numbers were exposed

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Only above 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested; Appendix B III.A allows the same delay for member notice

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the credit union (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (for example the MSP, the core processor, or the imaging server's tenant)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts; the credit union still sends notices (App. B II.A.2)

obligation: State data breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of another state (for example members who moved away)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the residency of every affected member; 14 in the worked example live outside Florida

obligation: Fidelity bond and cyber insurance notice
citation: Fidelity bond (12 CFR Part 713 coverage) and cyber policy (contracts)
trigger: Loss or suspected loss from fraud or a security incident
deadline: Per policy terms; notify before hiring response vendors; use panel counsel and forensics
notify: Bond carrier and the cyber insurer's 24x7 breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. The cyber policy's social engineering sublimit is $100,000

obligation: Banking organization notification incident
trigger: Notification incident at a bank or bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - applies to banking organizations, not credit unions. The NCUA 72-hour rule (748.1(c)) applies instead

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: No - the FTC rule reaches non-federally insured credit unions; this credit union is federally insured and supervised by NCUA

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity
deadline: As promptly as possible, no later than 72 hours after determining an incident occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - not New York-chartered or licensed

obligation: NYDFS extortion (ransom) payment
trigger: Extortion payment by a NYDFS-regulated entity
deadline: Notice within 24 hours of payment; written justification within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: No - not New York-chartered or licensed

obligation: SEC Reg S-P customer notification
trigger: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information at a broker-dealer, investment company, investment adviser, or transfer agent
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 30 days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: No - no SEC-registered broker-dealer or adviser

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event (in states adopting Model #668)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: As promptly as possible, no later than 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the credit union holds no insurance license

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - a member-owned credit union is not an SEC registrant

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Whether the final criteria would reach this credit union will be checked when a final rule is published

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not in a BEC incident (no ransom); kept for extortion scenarios (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the credit union holds no federal contracts
